sections.h2: Who assesses and who collects property tax in Jessamine County?
sections.html:
Two offices split the job. The Jessamine County Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values every parcel, and the Jessamine County Sheriff mails the bills and takes the payments.

The PVA's own duties page says the office does not set tax rates, does not send bills and does not collect a dollar. It assesses property at 100 percent of fair cash value as of January 1, keeps track of deed transfers, updates parcel maps and processes exemptions. The sheriff, whose office is at 201 North Main Street in Nicholasville and open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM, collects the state, county, school and district taxes on real and tangible property and passes each share to the proper taxing body.

If you want to change what you owe, the PVA is the office to call about value. If you want to know what you owe, call the sheriff at (859) 885-4139.

sections.h2: How has Jessamine County's assessed value changed?
sections.html:
Total assessments have climbed every year since 2013, and the 2026 roll rose 9.00 percent to about $6.71 billion. Residential property carries most of that weight at roughly $5.22 billion, with commercial at about $1.04 billion and agricultural at about $444 million.

A seller reading this sees why a house bought a few years ago may now carry a much larger assessment. Growth of that size usually comes from rising sales prices and new construction at the same time, and the PVA's roll captures both. Because each class is reassessed on a four-year cycle, a big step in one year can reflect several years of price movement landing together.

sections.h2: What property classes does the Jessamine County PVA use?
sections.html:
The PVA sorts taxable property into four classes, and each is reassessed on a four-year cycle or sooner if the office sees a reason. Which class your house falls in depends mostly on where it sits and how much land comes with it.

  • Residential: homes inside the city limits of Nicholasville and Wilmore, including single-family houses, duplexes, townhouses and vacant lots.
  • County Residential: homes or vacant land outside those cities on less than 10 acres, which may include trailers, barns and sheds.
  • Farms: tracts of 10 acres or more, which is also where agricultural value is determined.
  • Commercial and Industrial: businesses on commercial or industrial ground, plus golf courses, apartment buildings and trailer park acreage.

Farm owners can ask for agricultural valuation on tracts of 10 acres or more by filing on or before March 1 of any year. Horticultural land qualifies at 5 acres. The PVA describes the use-value program as a way to keep farming operations going and preserve farmland through property tax relief.

sections.h2: When are Jessamine County tax bills due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Bills reach the sheriff by September 15, and the 2 percent discount applies through November 1. Face amount is due from November 2 through December 31. After that, a 5 percent penalty applies through January 31, and from February 1 a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's fee is added.

That schedule comes from the county PVA's tax calendar, which cites KRS 134.020 for the discount. The Kentucky Department of Revenue says bills still unpaid at the close of business on April 15 move to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency, with a lien recorded against the property. After that, interest of 1 percent per month and clerk and county attorney commissions pile on, and the clerk may hold a tax sale in the summer where a third party can buy the bill.

The clerk's website has a delinquent tax lookup. Confirm each year's exact dates with the sheriff, because the state allows a delayed schedule in some counties.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jessamine County assessment?
sections.html:
You must talk with the PVA first. Notices of assessment are usually mailed in April, and the inspection period begins on the first Monday in May and runs for the 13 days that follow, Saturdays included.

The PVA office takes conferences by phone or in person, and the number is (859) 885-4931. Dates are printed on the notice and published in the Jessamine Journal. Bring anything that supports a lower value, such as a recent appraisal, photos, an insurance policy, current listings or neighborhood sales.

  • Step 1: hold the PVA conference during the inspection period.
  • Step 2: if you do not agree, file an appeal form with the County Clerk no later than one workday after the inspection period ends. A three-member Board of Assessment Appeals then hears it.
  • Step 3: you may go on to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, whose members are appointed by the Governor.

The Department of Revenue adds that the local board sits between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes and denies appeals that arrive without factual evidence.

sections.h2: What tax relief can a Jessamine County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older, and owners declared totally disabled, may subtract a fixed amount from the assessed value of their home. The PVA's announcement lists the exemption at $49,100 for 2025 to 2026.

Only one exemption is allowed per household. Once approved, the age exemption stays in place for as long as the original applicant owns and lives in the house, and it moves with the person when they sell. The disability exemption works differently here, because the PVA says each recipient must reapply every year. Applications go in person to the PVA office or by mail to P.O. Box 530, Nicholasville, KY 40340, with a copy of a driver's license or birth certificate and, for disability, proof such as a Social Security award letter.

Churches and charities can apply for exemption on Revenue Form 62A023. Business owners also file tangible personal property returns by May 15, and late filers face 10 percent or 20 percent penalties.

sections.h2: What should I know about taxes when selling a Jessamine County house?
sections.html:
The bill follows the January 1 assessment, so the name on a September bill can be the previous owner. Settle the split at closing instead of waiting for the sheriff to sort it out.

Jessamine County keeps adding people and housing. Census data puts the median owner-occupied home value at $268,100 for 2020 to 2024, the owner-occupancy rate at 66.7 percent and the July 2025 population estimate at 57,147, up 7.8 percent since the 2020 count. Housing units numbered 22,061 as of July 2025.

Before listing, ask the sheriff for a payoff on the current bill and check the clerk's delinquent search for old ones. A seller who holds the age exemption should tell the PVA about the sale so the benefit can move to the next home.

faqs.q: Does the Jessamine County PVA send my property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The PVA sets the assessed value only. The Jessamine County Sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the PVA's duties page says its office does not set rates or collect taxes.

faqs.q: What is the last day to get the 2 percent discount in Jessamine County?
faqs.a: November 1. The discount comes from KRS 134.020 and applies to bills paid on or before that date, after which the face amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: When does an unpaid Jessamine County tax bill go to the clerk?
faqs.a: At the close of business on April 15. The sheriff transfers it to the Jessamine County Clerk, a lien is recorded and interest of 1 percent per month begins.

faqs.q: How much is the Jessamine County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The PVA lists $49,100 for 2025 to 2026. It applies to owners 65 or older who live in the home, and the amount is adjusted every two years.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Jessamine County assessment after the bill arrives?
faqs.a: Not through the normal route. The PVA conference and the County Clerk filing both happen in May, so the window closes before bills go out in the fall.
